```js
const banNewDate = {
    selector: "NewExpression[callee.name='Date']",
    message: 'Use the clock module instead of new Date().',
};

export default [
    {
        rules: {
            'no-restricted-syntax': ['error', banNewDate],
        },
    },
    {
        files: ['src/**/*.js'],
        ignores: ['src/auth/**'],
        rules: {
            'no-restricted-syntax': [
                'error',
                banNewDate,
                {
                    selector: 'ImportDeclaration[source.value=/auth.internal/]',
                    message: 'Import auth through src/auth/index.js, never its internals.',
                },
            ],
        },
    },
];
```

Two parts of the structure are deliberate:
- **Separate global block:** the existing block skips `src/auth/**`, so a rule added only there would miss auth.
- **Selector listed twice, global block first:** a later `no-restricted-syntax` replaces earlier options instead of merging. If the global block came last, it would silently remove the auth import ban.

**What I found**
- The ban reaches every file ESLint lints, and it matches all `new Date(...)` forms, including `new Date(someValue)`. To allow parsing and block only current-time reads, add `[arguments.length=0]` to the selector.
- Nothing in `src/` calls `new Date()`, so the rule should add no violations.
- The rule hasn't been seen to fail yet, so the next step is to prove it (the record calls this PROVE).

**Why it matters**
- **Lint is probably already red:** `src/billing/invoice.js:1` imports `../auth/internal/token.js`, which breaks the existing auth rule. I left that alone. Don't read a green lint run as success unless that import has been fixed, because a green run could also mean the auth rule got shadowed.
- **No clock module in this repo:** if it gets added here and calls `new Date()`, this rule will flag it, and it will need its own exemption block. If it's an external package, nothing changes.
- **Other ways to read the time:** `Date.now()`, `Date()` without `new`, and `new globalThis.Date()` all still pass.
